components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid ember-orange button for the primary action on a screen or modal.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: inherit; background: #e8792f; color: #1a1008; border: 1px solid #e8792f; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-weight: bold; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #f5893f; border-color: #f5893f; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f5893f; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Baseline button treatment every raw <button> gets by default.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font: inherit; color: #f2ede8; background: #292320; border: 1px solid #3a332e; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #e8792f; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e8792f; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive-action button; inverts to solid red on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { font: inherit; background: #fbe3e3; border: 1px solid #cc0000; color: #cc0000; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #cc0000; color: #fff; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #cc0000; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card Search Input
components.description: Search/filter text input used across search and filter toolbars.
components.css: .ds-input { font: inherit; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #3a332e; background: #1e1a17; color: #f2ede8; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #a89e96; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3fc4d1; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #3fc4d1; }

components.name: Result Card
components.description: Compact card used in the card-search results grid; image, name, printing metadata.
components.css: .ds-card-result { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; background: #1e1a17; border: 1px solid #3a332e; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.5rem; text-align: center; transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-card-result:hover, .ds-card-result:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(232, 121, 47, 0.35); } .ds-card-image { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 5 / 7; max-width: 200px; border-radius: 4px; background: #292320; } .ds-card-name { font-weight: bold; margin: 0; color: #f2ede8; } .ds-card-printing { color: #a89e96; font-size: 0.75rem; margin: 0; }

components.name: Color Identity Pip
components.description: Signature component: WUBRG color-identity pips using Magic's traditional print colors, deliberately outside the app's own token palette.

components.css: .ds-color-identity { display: inline-flex; gap: 0.25rem; } .ds-pip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1.5rem; height: 1.5rem; border-radius: 50%; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: bold; color: #999; background: #eee; border: 1px solid #ccc; } .ds-pip.filled { color: #fff; border-color: transparent; } .ds-pip-w.filled { background: #f8f6d8; color: #333; } .ds-pip-u.filled { background: #0e68ab; } .ds-pip-b.filled { background: #150b00; } .ds-pip-r.filled { background: #d3202a; } .ds-pip-g.filled { background: #00733e; }

narrative.overview:
Grimorio's interface reads like a spellbook studied by candlelight: a near-black page (#14110f) that recedes into the dark, warmed by a single ember-orange accent that behaves like the only light source in the room. The mood is moody and mysterious — closer to the game's fantasy atmosphere than to a typical productivity dashboard — and deliberately avoids anything playful or cartoonish. Depth is not conveyed by flat tonal steps alone; interactive surfaces are meant to feel lifted and lit, gaining a soft ember glow as they're touched, the way an object catches candlelight as a hand moves near it.

The palette stays restrained by design: orange is the one warm voice, used sparingly for primary actions and brand marks, while a cool spectral teal appears only for links and active navigation state, playing the role of a faint enchantment against the fire-toned foreground. Everything else — surfaces, borders, muted text — lives in a narrow band of warm near-blacks and browns, so the two accent colors read as genuinely rare, not just "the palette."
keyCharacteristics: Near-black warm background, never a cool/blue-tinted dark
Single warm accent (ember orange) carries primary actions and brand identity
Cool teal accent is reserved and sparing — navigation/links only
Elevation is atmospheric: glow and shadow, not flat color-step layering alone

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: Ember Orange is the only warm accent and should stay rare — primary CTAs and the brand mark, not decoration. If a screen has more than one orange element competing for attention, that's a hierarchy bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The No-Display-Font Rule
rules.body: There is currently no dedicated display/heading typeface — don't introduce one ad hoc in a single component. If a display face becomes a real product decision, it belongs in a dedicated pass that updates this token set project-wide.

rules.name: The Candlelight Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the accent color, not from a generic gray shadow. When adding elevation to a new interactive element, prefer a soft glow tinted with --color-primary (or --color-accent for teal-toned elements) over a neutral rgba(0,0,0,…) shadow.

dos: Do use the ember-orange glow (derived from --color-primary) for hover/focus on primary interactive elements as elevation work continues — the confirmed direction, even where not yet implemented.
Do treat the add-card modal (add-card-modal.scss) as the reference pattern for new modals — token-based, mobile full-bleed, fixed header/scrollable body.
Do keep Ember Orange rare — primary CTAs and brand mark only (The One Flame Rule).
Do keep the five MTG color-identity pip colors as their traditional print colors, not tokens from the app's own palette — they need to stay recognizable to players.
donts: Don't introduce a second warm accent color competing with Ember Orange; the palette's restraint is the point.
Don't use neutral gray/black shadows for new interactive elevation — prefer a color-tinted glow per The Candlelight Rule.

Don't copy hardcoded hex/px values from older components (entity-list, card-list, dashboard-panel, auth-modal) into new work — they predate the token system in _tokens.scss; use the CSS custom properties instead.
Don't introduce a display/heading typeface in a single component ad hoc (The No-Display-Font Rule) — it's a project-wide decision, not yet made.
